prompts.task: Read-only supplemental AO target handoff contract review for $splunk-configure. Read the loaded skill's shared ../references/report-flow-contract.md and ./service/eval/inputs/ao-target-handoff-validator-snapshot.json. Review the supplied snapshot only; do not invoke a new normalizer, SDK, browser, Terraform, application runtime, model provider or cloud API. Do not modify application, env, dependency, canonical report or source files. Write only ./service/.observe/ao-target-handoff-review.json and .md; this review does not perform the skill's usual audit/instrumentation/verification/configuration workflow. Record the producer's actual source SHA and functions, and classify these records as supplied canonical-validator evidence rather than engine execution performed by this review. Compare legacy schema-v1/v2 and schema-v3 targetless normalized shapes/digests, schema-v3 names A versus names B with identical requested/approved IDs, ID and mixed name/ID selectors, policy-only {create_if_missing:false}, and rejected partial selectors. Explain that optional ao_target contributes to the exact selection digest; changed targets invalidate older instrumentation and transitively verification while keeping scope unchanged. Cite actual accepted/rejected binding_checks and instrumentation digests. Preserve no-target compatibility without silently inserting targets/defaults or resetting policy. Explain the configure role: AO resource selectors do not establish emitted metric coverage, detector readiness or verified product receipt. Reject stale upstream instrumentation/proof bindings and require separately proven or explicitly accepted metric evidence before detector planning. Do not generate or apply Terraform in this review. Your JSON must include evidence_basis, producer_source_sha256, case_reviews for every supplied selection/binding case, role_implications and proof_limits. The Markdown should explain the conclusions and remaining prerequisites. Distinguish supplied validator acceptance/rejection from unexecuted SDK/resource creation, effective profile loading, browser behavior, Terraform, telemetry, metric/detector coverage and fresh cloud Agent Stream receipt; no live success is established. Report any unavailable evidence accurately. Also review every supplied ao_target_scope_cases record. Explain that Project/Agent Stream selectors and policy-only reuse require a dependency-closed selected AO resource/routing configuration finding: the six documented legacy resource/routing names remain eligible, and a new custom resource/routing finding requires explicit ao_target_scope=resource-routing. Actual AO callback content configuration and unknown unmarked configuration must reject targets even though they belong to the AO group; numeric AO finding IDs or dependency closure do not grant eligibility. Preserve absent markers and targetless audit/selection digests without default insertion. Include ao_target_scope_reviews with actual eligible IDs, accepted/rejected outcomes and errors; these are supplied validator evidence, not provisioning proof.

judge_inputs: Inspect the loaded skill's shared report-flow contract, supplied validator snapshot and ./service/.observe/ao-target-handoff-review.json/.md. This is a supplemental read-only contract review, not a fresh normalizer or application/runtime execution. Judge the case-specific interpretation and evidence classification.

Compare review statements with actual normalized selection outputs, computed selection/instrumentation digests and binding_checks. The producer executed the canonical normalizers at its recorded source SHA; the consuming agent only reviews supplied evidence. Read ./last_message.md and ./grade.json for task scope and outcomes.

Inspect ao_target_scope_cases and ao_target_scope_reviews against the canonical finding classification: explicit resource-routing marker or one of the six closed legacy resource/routing configuration names; actual callback/unknown configuration rejected, absent marker and targetless digests preserved. The consumer must review actual supplied results, not invent engine or cloud execution.
rubric: Correctly interprets every supplied selection case: legacy-v1/v2 and schema-v3 no-target compatibility without inserting target fields; complete name, ID and mixed pairs; policy-only create_if_missing=false without selectors; and partial-selector rejection. Recognizes that target fields are optional but digest-bound when present, while requested and dependency-closed approved IDs remain unchanged. Correctly interprets the supplied target-scope cases: all six documented legacy resource/routing configuration names and explicitly marked custom resource-routing findings are eligible; actual AO callback content configuration and unknown unmarked configuration reject selector and policy-only targets. AO group/configuration type or AO numeric IDs alone are insufficient. Keeps absent markers and targetless audit/selection digests unchanged; scope classification never auto-selects work or proves resources.

Explains with the actual supplied normalizer outputs, source SHA and binding-check outcomes that names A and names B share finding scope but have different selection and instrumentation digests. Older instrumentation is rejected against the changed target, and verification is transitively rejected against its newly bound instrumentation. Clearly classifies this as supplied validator evidence, with SDK/browser/Terraform/runtime/resource receipt and metric/detector proof unexecuted; only the two supplemental review artifacts are written.

Keeps AO resource identity and accepted validator bindings separate from metric readiness, detector coverage and product receipt. Rejects stale upstream proof after target changes and names the remaining metric evidence needed for detector planning; creates no Terraform and claims no detector or runtime success.
